description:
RESTATED 2026-09-02 from the measured population at main a3a9761d1
(proposal + cold review with prototype; the original 'enum_map_family/00277
+6-9% native code' premise is refuted: neither fixture carries a same-callee
contained arm pair at main; both are define_function 827->827 / 784->784
under the prototype).

THE DEFECT. fz-kdt.118's drop runs only WITHIN a question group
(callsite_dispatch.rs unroutable_alternatives takes `groups`). Every axis
refinement since (119 tuples, 125/127 callables, 107.3 list heads) turned
each same-callee contained pair into TWO questions, so at main the group-
local drop fires on ZERO corpus pairs (census: 66 same-callee contained
pairs on 9 fixtures, no two sharing a question, none dropped). The un-
dropped narrow arm is then either DEAD (seated after the arm that stands in
for it) or a HAZARD: the insertion seat stops at the first refusal, so on an
arrival that puts a neither-covers pair between them the narrow arm stays
ahead and `[1, :ok]` reaches the int-reading body. Measured: under
FZ_STRESS_PERMUTE_DISPATCH=arms:2/3 the blind-escape census reports 5 where
the settled order pins 3, the extras being `[int]` / `[int | :ok]` ahead of
their stand-ins on dispatch_list_head_separates.

THE RULE.
  unroutable(N)  <=>  exists W != N : stands_in_for(W, N) and not seats_before(N, W)
  stands_in_for(W, N) := same callee, surface(N) strictly inside surface(W),
                          test(N) contained in test(W)
  seats_before(x, y)  := covers(x, y) and (not covers(y, x) or strictly_inside(x, y))
                         -- specificity_order's own relation, factored into one
                            free function both the drop and the seat call.
For a stand-in pair covers(W, N) holds unconditionally, so keep N iff
covers(N, W) and strictly_inside(test N, test W): a redundant arm survives
only where the seat itself would put it ahead of its stand-in. Tests equal
=> strictly_inside false => dropped: fz-kdt.118 exactly, on its population.
The rule's population BEYOND 118's is exactly {N : some W stands in and not
covers(N, W)}, and not-covers(N, W) is by definition 'seating N first is a
blind escape' -- the predicate drive_test::blind_escapes counts. So nothing
the seat would put first is ever dropped (review CE-10/CE-11; measured: all
39 dropped corpus arms sit strictly behind their stand-in, none at seat 0).
The test-containment conjunct is LOAD-BEARING and NOT implied by surface
containment: `[int | :ok] & not([:ok])` vs `[int | :ok]` -- the negated
list clause degrades to shape_only, so the narrower surface carries the
WIDER test; without the conjunct that arm is dropped and `[:zzz]` moves to
an outcome no legal arrival produced (review CE-8; pinned as a unit gate).
Relative soundness, stated properly: take the arrival [survivors in post-
drop seated order, then dropped arms widest-first]; the first k insertions
reproduce the survivors' seat verbatim, and each dropped N cannot pass its
stand-in W (that needs seats_before(N, W), false by the drop condition), so
N receives nothing -- every post-drop routing is one that legal arrival
produced.

MEASURED YIELD (prototype, base -> proto): canon movers exactly 4;
dispatch sites 51 -> 51 (no Dispatch->Direct collapse on the corpus), arms
126 -> 106. receive_map_pattern / receive_list_cons_pattern /
receive_interleaved_tuple_arity: 6 of 8 Kernel.dbg/1 arms dropped each
(fz-kdt.140's 2^arity product), define_function 46->34 / 49->37 / 49->37,
executables 25->13 each. dispatch_list_head_separates: arms 4 -> 2, plan-
only (x32/x33 List.reduce_while_cont/3 over list(int|:ok)/list(int) stay
demanded through the callable-flow path). Escape census: settled 3 -> 3;
arms:2/3 5 -> 3; arms:6 7 -> 5 -- the two arms:6 survivors are
enum_predicate_search's `[int]` (whose CALLABLE surface is strictly WIDER
than its sibling's: containment one way at subject 0, the other way at
subject 2 = fz-kdt.131 facet 3, structurally out of this rule's reach).
Behaviour 0 movers on interp/JIT (597) and AOT (the 4 movers); stress
arms:reverse/1/6 identical.

RIP OUT IN THE SAME COMMIT: unroutable_alternatives' `groups` parameter and
the question_groups call that fed it; the inline seats_before closure;
specificity_order re-projecting questions/groups (project once, pass the
survivors' questions down); the 'within one question group' law in every
doc (callsite_dispatch.rs, dispatch-matrix.md 55-140 and ~372, question_
groups' doc, drive_test.rs census SCOPE note / ARM_ORDER_CENSUS /
BLIND_ESCAPE_POPULATION docs, fixture headers of the 4 movers incl.
budget.codegen.functions 46->34/49->37/49->37 with cause); three unit
tests REWRITTEN (a_narrower_twin_becomes_an_arm_once_the_test_can_tell_it_
apart -> Direct(wide); an_arm_whose_head_overlaps_a_wider_one_is_seated_
after_it -> Direct(wide) both arrivals; a_list_head_seats_the_covering_arm_
and_leaves_the_inseparable_pair_as_it_arrived -> C gone on all six
arrivals). New gates: the 118 subset stated directly (one question on an
erasing axis, strict surfaces -> Direct); precision boundary (int vs
int|float -> both, narrow first); CE-8 (shape_only-degraded narrow arm is
NOT dropped). Escape-census gate restated as per-setting named constants
(settled 3; arms:6 adds the two enum_predicate_search entries owned by
131) -- NOT as an arrival-invariant claim. Record: the rule reaches
sole_destination's fail-node removal across the whole arm set where 118
reached it only within a group (corpus impact 0; fenced by the semantic
analysis). Correct in passing the stale drive_test.rs doc (~9573) claiming
four fixtures still abort natively under seeds -- all 28 combinations exit
0 at main.

SEQUENCE: before fz-kdt.168 (whose one-sided covers un-drops exact-vs-any
closure arms with no edit here; its a_mixed instance is stale at main: 0
call-dispatch sites). fz-kdt.140's measured population becomes 11 -> 13 per
receive fixture, cause unchanged (the minting).

comments.text: SAFETY DIMENSION added by the fz-kdt.107 step-3 refutation (2026-09-02, cc fz-kdt.131): losing fz-kdt.118's drop when a question group splits is not only +native code -- an un-dropped narrow list arm is a NEW BLIND-ESCAPE SEAT under legal arrivals base could never produce. Measured: under arms:3 the head-refined trio callsite's census reports 5 escapes where the settled order pins 3; the two extras are [int]-before-[int|:ok|:true] and [int]-before-[int|:ok] -- seatings impossible at base because 118 dropped both narrow arms (only two destinations settled). Zero behavior impact today (585x2-door + 30 seeds x JIT + 8 x AOT all clean), and the settled-order census is structurally blind to it (scope note added to the gate); fz-kdt.141's stress is the instrument that sees them. This ticket's cure (test-containment drop) closes the seats, not just the bytes.

title: A redundant arm survives only where the seat would put it ahead of its stand-in: the drop is the seating relation read the other way
